edges.reason: Likelihood is defined from a probabilistic model of observed data given parameters.
Sampling from a model requires understanding distributions and randomness represented by probabilistic models.
Supervised prediction methods require understanding how inputs, features, and labels are represented.
Neural networks require data to be encoded as numerical vectors, tensors, or other structured representations.
Training algorithms commonly rely on optimization concepts to adjust model parameters and minimize objectives.
